title: Markets: Friday 6 November

morning.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · before the 10:00 open
summary: The S&P 500 fell 4.3% and the Nasdaq 5.4% ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-stocks-lower-at-close-of-trade-dow-jones-industrial-average-down-345-5005517)), erasing Wednesday's post-election gains. Brent futures rose 4.0% to US$98.42 (snapshot) as attacks on tankers in the Gulf continued ([Reuters via CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/oil-jumps-over-3-investors-assess-iran-war-future-tanker-attacks-6526116)).

S&P/ASX 200 futures pointed to a fall of between 33 and 66 points at the open, depending on when they were read ([Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com.au/2026/11/06/5-things-to-watch-on-the-asx-200-on-friday-06-november-2026/); [AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-steady-nasdaq-plunges-on-ai-regulation-fears-20261106-p61bvd)), after the index rose 2.6% to 9,065.1 on Thursday (snapshot). Tech and miners led that rise, so they are most exposed to the US chip sell-off, while higher oil supports energy producers.

Macquarie reports its half-year result today, with Morgan Stanley forecasting a 29% rise in profit to A$2.14 billion ([Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com.au/2026/11/06/5-things-to-watch-on-the-asx-200-on-friday-06-november-2026/)). US October payrolls follow at 12:30am Saturday Sydney time; the FactSet consensus is 65,000 jobs, after 29,000 in September ([Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/economy/october-jobs-report-seen-showing-resilient-labor-market)).

cards.headline: Wall Street gives back its post-election rally as chip stocks slump
cards.takeaway: The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell about 11% as investors weighed whether Democratic wins will slow US data-centre construction.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Yesterday covered Wednesday's rally, when chip and data-centre stocks already lagged. New: the selling spread to the whole market, and all 11 S&P 500 sectors fell.
cards.what_happened: The S&P 500 closed 4.3% lower, the Nasdaq 5.4% and the Dow 3.5% ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-stocks-lower-at-close-of-trade-dow-jones-industrial-average-down-345-5005517)). The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell as much as 11.2% to its lowest in more than six months; Nvidia fell 9% and AMD 15% ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ai-datacenter-stocks-slip-as-democratic-sweep-clouds-expansion-plans-5003196)). Qualcomm fell 10% after a weaker-than-expected outlook, all 11 S&P 500 sectors traded lower, and the VIX touched 28.09, its highest since 31 March ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Voters sided against data centres in every one of 41 local ballot measures on Tuesday except one, in Harwood, North Dakota ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/data-center-ballot-measures-2026-midterm.html)). Senator Bernie Sanders posted "National data center moratorium now", and Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said in October she would pause data-centre approvals ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/democrats-data-center-restrictions-midterms.html)). UBS estimated about 30% of expected 2028 US data-centre additions could be affected by construction pauses ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ai-datacenter-stocks-slip-as-democratic-sweep-clouds-expansion-plans-5003196)). State Street strategists noted that a Democratic Congress alone could not curtail construction against a presidential veto, and that AI remains a priority for both parties ([Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/new-political-landscape-facing-ai-after-democrats-midterm-gains)). For Australia, the RBA said on Tuesday that AI-related investment has lifted growth in major trading partners and that data-centre investment supports local business investment ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/media-releases/2026/mr-26-30.html)); on the ASX, tech and materials led Thursday's rise.
cards.market_reaction: Treasuries rallied and gold rose (see the Fed card). The S&P 500, Nasdaq and VIX tiles still show Wednesday''s closes, because Thursday's session ended after the 7:30am cutoff (snapshot).

competing_views.view: Said the slowdown is "a negative for Semis and AI infrastructure, but a lot is already priced into Semis with valuations nearing multi-year lows".
Said "the shakeout in A.I.-related stocks has much further to run" and recommended diversifying away from tech.
Said volatility "has not yet reached the capitulation or contrarian extremes historically associated with capitulation points".

cards.what_to_watch: How ASX tech and data-centre names open after Thursday's gains, and US payrolls at 12:30am Saturday.

cards.headline: Brent rebounds 4% as tanker attacks keep Gulf supply risk alive
cards.takeaway: Oil recovered part of Wednesday's 8.7% fall as more vessels were hit near the Strait of Hormuz and no US–Iran deal was announced.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Yesterday Brent had settled 8.7% lower at US$94.62. New: a rebound driven by fresh tanker attacks and doubts about a quick deal.
cards.what_happened: Brent futures were at US$98.42 a barrel, up 4.0%, at 7:23am AEDT (snapshot). Brent settled US$3.67, or 3.9%, higher at US$98.29 in New York and WTI settled US$2.40, or 2.7%, higher at US$90.52 ([Reuters via CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/oil-jumps-over-3-investors-assess-iran-war-future-tanker-attacks-6526116)). At least five vessels have reported incidents since Sunday, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency, close to October's pace, when 35 vessels were hit ([Reuters via CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/oil-jumps-over-3-investors-assess-iran-war-future-tanker-attacks-6526116)).
cards.why_it_matters: Fuel is part of the consumer price index the RBA targets. The RBA said on Tuesday there are indications higher fuel prices are being passed through to other prices ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/media-releases/2026/mr-26-30.html)). Energy was the weakest ASX sector on Thursday as oil fell ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-thursday-5th-november)), so producers such as Woodside and Santos are the most direct beneficiaries of the rebound.

competing_views.view: Said "Today’s rebound reflects caution about pricing in a rapid normalization of oil flows before diplomatic progress translates into dependable shipping and deliveries".
Said in a note that any escalation could push Brent into a US$110 to US$125 a barrel range.

cards.what_to_watch: Any US response to Iran's latest proposal (see the Iran card), and further tanker incidents.

comparison.title: Which Brent price?
comparison.why_different: The snapshot carries two Brent series. The EIA spot assessment is published with a lag of several days and still reflects 3 November, before Wednesday's fall; the futures price is the front-month contract quoted in most news reports. They measure different things on different dates and should not be compared as a daily move.

cards.headline: ASX 200 futures point lower after Thursday's 2.6% rise
cards.takeaway: Futures fell less than Wall Street, pointing to a drop of between 0.35% and 0.7% depending on the time of the read.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Thursday's Close tab gave 9,058.5 from a 4:01pm read and flagged an unresolved gap with the ABC's 9,065.1. The final close in this morning's snapshot is 9,065.1, so that gap is now explained as an earlier read before the closing auction.
cards.what_happened: The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 9,065.1 on Thursday, up 2.6% (snapshot). SPI futures were down 49 points (0.5%) at 6:21am AEDT ([SMH](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/wall-street-plunges-as-ai-stocks-tumble-asx-set-to-slide-lower-20261106-p61bvl.html)), down 33 points (0.35%) in a Motley Fool read cited at 7:13am ([Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com.au/2026/11/06/5-things-to-watch-on-the-asx-200-on-friday-06-november-2026/)) and down 66 points (0.7%) to 9,012 near 7:50am ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-steady-nasdaq-plunges-on-ai-regulation-fears-20261106-p61bvd)). The Australian dollar was at US$0.7014 at the RBA's 4pm fix on Thursday (snapshot) and at US69.52 cents early this morning ([SMH](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/wall-street-plunges-as-ai-stocks-tumble-asx-set-to-slide-lower-20261106-p61bvl.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Thursday's gain was led by tech and materials, with NextDC up more than 40% at midday after Goodman and Digital Realty built a stake, while energy and financials fell ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-thursday-5th-november)). NextDC closed 48% higher ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)). Those are the sectors most exposed to the US chip and data-centre sell-off, while energy producers may gain from oil's rebound.
cards.what_to_watch: Macquarie's result (see the next card), and whether the ASX holds up better than Wall Street, as the futures suggest.

comparison.title: How far are ASX futures down?
comparison.why_different: SPI futures kept trading while Wall Street was still open, so each outlet captured a different moment. The figures are all the same contract at different times, not conflicting measures.

cards.headline: Macquarie reports its half-year result on Wikramanayake's last day as CEO
cards.takeaway: Brokers expect strong profit growth; Greg Ward takes over as chief executive on Saturday.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Previously listed only in the calendar. New: the result is due today, with broker forecasts.
cards.what_happened: Macquarie reports its result for the six months to 30 September today ([Macquarie](https://www.macquarie.com/au/en/investors.html)). Shemara Wikramanayake retires as managing director and CEO effective 6 November, and Greg Ward, head of Banking and Financial Services, joins the boards effective 7 November ([Macquarie](https://www.macquarie.com/au/en/about/news/2026/shemara-wikramanayake-to-retire-in-november-2026-greg-ward-to-become-managing-director-and-ceo-of-macquarie-group.html)). Full-year profit to 31 March was A$4,847 million, up 30% ([Kalkine](https://kalkine.com.au/news/financial/asx-today-macquarie-group-asxmqg-prepares-to-report-half-year-result-on-6-november)).
cards.why_it_matters: Macquarie's commodities and markets business trades energy, so the half covers a volatile period for oil and gas prices. It is also the next big financial result after NAB shares fell sharply on Thursday after higher bad-debt charges ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/nab-fy26-result-shares-head-for-worst-day-since-february-2025-as-bad-debts-nearly-double)).

competing_views.view: Forecasts a 29% rise in half-year profit to A$2.14 billion.
Expects return on equity of 13.4%, ahead of consensus estimates.

cards.what_to_watch: The interim dividend and outlook commentary; shares go ex-dividend on 11 November.

cards.headline: Treasury yields fall and December Fed hike bets ease
cards.takeaway: Investors moved into bonds as stocks fell, even though jobless claims and productivity data were strong.
cards.key_figure: US 2Y yield down more than 11bp to 4.466% (CNBC, intraday 5 Nov)
cards.what_happened: The 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 5bp to 4.839% and the 2-year more than 11bp to 4.466% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/treasury-yields-bonds-interest-rates.html)); yields reached their lowest since early September ([Bloomberg via Mint](https://www.livemint.com/market/treasuries-soar-as-tech-stock-selloff-lures-investors-to-havens-11793908983146.html)). Initial jobless claims fell 6,000 to 189,000, below the Dow Jones estimate of 197,000, and third-quarter productivity rose 3.6%, ahead of the 2.9% estimate, while unit labour costs fell 0.7% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)). Gold futures rose 1.1% to US$4,115.9 (snapshot).
cards.why_it_matters: Lower US yields and a weaker case for a December hike can lift the Australian dollar and support Australian bonds. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin both expressed support for higher rates on Thursday ([Bloomberg via Mint](https://www.livemint.com/market/treasuries-soar-as-tech-stock-selloff-lures-investors-to-havens-11793908983146.html)).
cards.market_reaction: The US 10Y and 2Y tiles show Wednesday's official readings (scheduled lag); Thursday's moves are from CNBC.

cards.headline: US October payrolls due early Saturday; forecasts range widely
cards.takeaway: Published consensus figures sit between 55,000 and 65,000 jobs, with unemployment expected to hold at 4.2%.
cards.what_happened: The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the October jobs report at 8:30am US Eastern on Friday, 12:30am Saturday Sydney time. September payrolls rose 29,000 and unemployment rose to 4.2%. Forecasters expect unemployment to stay at 4.2% and average hourly earnings to rise 0.3% ([Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/economy/october-jobs-report-seen-showing-resilient-labor-market)).
cards.why_it_matters: Economists quoted by Morningstar said the report is unlikely to change expectations for a December Fed hike, though a strong result could add to bets on hikes early next year. A softer result after Thursday's sell-off could weaken the US dollar further.

comparison.title: What is the payrolls consensus?
comparison.why_different: Each figure comes from a different survey of economists, taken at a different time. Westpac's calendar carries the Bloomberg consensus as at its late-October publication. None is wrong; they are different polls.

competing_views.view: Expects 120,000 jobs, well above consensus, citing positive momentum in private-sector data.
Expects about 74,000 jobs and calls the labour market "relatively robust, but frozen".

cards.what_to_watch: The unemployment rate and wages, alongside the headline jobs number.

cards.headline: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4%, its first rise since 2023
cards.takeaway: The vote was 8–1, with the dissenter wanting a bigger rise, and Governor Bailey tied further moves to the Middle East conflict.
cards.key_figure: Bank Rate 4.00%, up from 3.75% (Bank of England, 5 Nov)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Yesterday previewed the decision. New: the result, the vote and the Bank's guidance.
cards.what_happened: The Monetary Policy Committee voted 8–1 to raise Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4%, with Catherine Mann voting for a 0.5-point rise. The Bank said UK inflation, 3.5% in September, is expected to rise to around 5% by the middle of next year ([Bank of England](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy-summary-and-minutes/2026/november-2026)). Governor Andrew Bailey said the move "shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes", but "unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase" ([BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ck5ynw45jrgqo)).
cards.why_it_matters: The Fed and the ECB raised rates before the BoE in this energy shock ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/bank-of-england-poised-to-raise-rates-but-may-push-back-on-bets-for-more-4989788)), and the RBA raised on Tuesday. The FTSE 100 fell 0.4% after the decision ([SMH, AP](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/wall-street-plunges-as-ai-stocks-tumble-asx-set-to-slide-lower-20261106-p61bvl.html)).

competing_views.view: Suggested additional hikes may be likely, depending on how inflation affects wages, prices and jobs.
Described the rise as "a risk-management 'one-for-now' insurance hike".

cards.headline: RBA's Hauser says confidence in near-term inflation delivery has fallen
cards.takeaway: Overall trust is broadly stable at about 55%, he said, but confidence in the bank's near-term ability to meet its objectives "has fallen materially".
cards.what_happened: In the Sir Leslie Melville Lecture on Thursday evening, Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said around 55% of respondents to the RBA's Community Research Survey have high or moderately high trust in the bank, a broadly stable figure, but trust in its near-term ability to meet its objectives "has fallen materially". He said companies in the Macquarie University BOSS survey have become less sure the inflation target will be met over the next 5–10 years, and that Australians with a mortgage have considerably lower trust than those without. Describing how monetary policy works, he said "pain often precedes gain" ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/sp-dg-2026-11-05.html)). The speech came days after the board raised the cash rate to 4.85% ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/policy/economy/pain-before-gain-hauser-defends-rba-rate-rises-20261105-p61blj)).
cards.why_it_matters: Hauser argued that when people trust the central bank, a smaller rate response is needed to bring inflation down. The board said on Tuesday there is "an increasing risk that higher inflation expectations will become embedded", and six members voted for the rise while three preferred to hold ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/media-releases/2026/mr-26-30.html)).

competing_views.view: Expect the cash rate to stay at 4.85% "for a while".

cards.what_to_watch: Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter speaks at 9:30am on Monday 9 November ([Westpac](https://library.westpaciq.com.au/content/dam/public/westpaciq/secure/economics/documents/aus/2026/10/Economic_Calendar_November_2026_WBC.pdf)).

cards.headline: More tankers hit near Hormuz as Iran sends a new proposal via Qatar
cards.takeaway: Iranian forces said several tankers caught fire after using unauthorised routes, while Washington is reviewing a Tehran proposal and Oman pressed for a shipping arrangement.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Yesterday covered US and Iranian reactions to the midterms. New: Thursday's tanker incidents, Iran's proposal and Oman's statement.
cards.what_happened: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire after trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz on unauthorised routes, one after striking a mine, and Iran's army later said three more tankers struck mines. Separately, UKMTO said a tanker was hit by two projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Qatar ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/5/iran-says-tankers-struck-in-hormuz-amid-fears-of-new-us-attack)). Tehran submitted a formal nuclear proposal to the United States through Qatar on Thursday, and Washington is reviewing it, according to officials cited by Reuters; its seven demands include compensation for war damage and an end to sanctions and the US naval blockade ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-israel-elections-november-5)). Oman said it and Iran discussed "joint technical mechanisms to secure the smooth flow of international trade and energy, in a manner that would end the state of war" ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/)).
cards.why_it_matters: Analysts say crude flows through the strait are close to pre-war levels, at higher cost ([Il Sole 24 Ore](https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/oil-prices-rise-again-brent-crude-above-95-gas-erases-losses-AJ2TEh5B)), but the attacks keep shipping risk in the oil price. In Washington, Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said the war "must end" and pointed to Congress's "power of the purse", while President Trump said "I would have done nothing different" ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/)).
cards.market_reaction: Brent futures +4.0% (snapshot); see the oil card.

competing_views.view: Said reports of tankers striking mines or being targeted by drones continue to worry the market, as does Iran's unchanged position on negotiations.

cards.what_to_watch: The US response to Iran's proposal, and whether tanker incidents continue at October's pace.

forecasts.view: Cash rate on hold at 4.85% "for a while".
